secret: The "monster" blamed for the attacks is no narwhal or sea creature but a man-made underwater boat of riveted steel plates, crewed by men, who drag Aronnax, Conseil and Ned Land inside.
The commander, who seemed not to understand the captives' story told in four languages, speaks perfect French and had understood them all along; he also speaks English, German and Latin.
The submarine is called the Nautilus; the N engraved on its tableware under the motto "Mobilis in Mobili" belongs to its name and its commander's.
The commander calls himself Captain Nemo (Latin for "no one"); he has cut himself off from humanity and will never let the three captives return to the world.

Nemo had the Nautilus's parts made by firms all over the world under different names, assembled it with his men on a deserted midocean islet, then burned every trace; he studied in London, Paris and New York and is immensely rich.
The coral clearing with its cross is the crew's secret cemetery on the seafloor, where Nemo's men bury their dead out of reach "of sharks and men"; the dead crewman was buried there.
Nemo says the poor pearl diver he saved lives in the land of the oppressed, and that he himself is, and will remain until his last breath, a native of that same land.
Nemo has discovered a secret undersea passage beneath the Isthmus of Suez, which he calls the Arabian Tunnel, linking the Red Sea to the Mediterranean.
The chest of gold Nemo sent off near Crete went to the Cretans rebelling against the Ottoman Empire; Nemo uses his wealth to help oppressed peoples and "victims to avenge".
Nemo's fortune comes from the treasure of the Spanish galleons sunk in the Bay of Vigo in 1702, and from countless other wrecks marked on his charts.
Nemo's stateroom holds portraits of heroes of liberation (Kosciusko, Botzaris, O'Connell, Washington, Manin, Lincoln, John Brown), suggesting he is a fighter for oppressed peoples.
The undersea ruins Nemo shows Aronnax are those of Atlantis; Nemo writes the word on a rock.
Nemo's secret home port lies inside a hollow extinct volcano, reached by an underwater passage, where the crew mine coal to make the sodium that powers the Nautilus.
At least one of the Nautilus's crew is French: the man carried off by the giant squid cries for help in French.
Nemo has written his research and his life story, signed with his real name, in a manuscript that the last survivor aboard will throw into the sea in an unsinkable case.
The spot Nemo searches for off Europe is the wreck of the Avenger (Vengeur), the French Republican warship that sank there in 1794 rather than surrender.

Nemo blames the nation of the warship that attacks the Nautilus for the destruction of his homeland, wife, children, father and mother; he sinks the ship with all hands, then weeps before a portrait of a young woman and two children.
The world's navies now know the "monster" is a submarine and are hunting it as an enemy.
Aronnax concludes that during the confinement in the Indian Ocean the Nautilus attacked a ship, and that the crewman buried in the coral cemetery was hurt in that collision; it is never confirmed.
Aronnax, Conseil and Ned Land escape in the skiff and survive the Maelstrom, waking in a fisherman's hut in the Lofoten Islands.

Nemo's real name, nationality and full past are never revealed, nor is the crew's language identified; the hints (the "land of the oppressed", the portraits) stay unconfirmed. Nothing may name his origin (e.g. India or Prince Dakkar) or mention a sequel.
The nationality of the warship Nemo sinks, and so of the nation he hates, is never revealed.
Whether the Nautilus survived the Maelstrom, whether Nemo lives, and whether his last words ("Enough! Enough!") mean repentance are left unknown.
